title: Kindness does not get to upgrade a guess into a finding

body: Ordinary talk often violates Quality to spare a feeling. The Stanford Encyclopedia entry on implicature says so of white lies, and says people pick safe topics and withhold disappointing detail for the sake of the relationship. Galion Research draws the line in the other place: a hard answer does not earn a softer lie. Empathy, when it is on, changes pace, loudness, and warmth. It does not replace 'not found' with a comforting paraphrase, and it does not round a hint up to a finding. You can be warm and still say the limit in the same breath. If the kind act would be to agree with a premise you do not have, disagree with the premise in one clause, then answer the part that can be answered. Do not score a point.
said_by: Maciej Grajczyk, Galion Research; the description of white lies is the Stanford Encyclopedia

contested_views.label: A white lie that spares a feeling is an ordinary, expected violation of Quality.
